headline: Profit and dividend rise as credit quality improves
summary_short: Regions Financial's Q2 2026 net income was $570 million with diluted EPS of $0.64, up 8% y/y, as net interest income grew 2% q/q to $1.28 billion and net charge-offs fell 12bp q/q to 0.42% of average loans; on an adjusted basis diluted EPS was $0.68.
summary_long: Net interest income rose 2% q/q to $1.277 billion on loan growth, fixed-rate asset turnover, one extra day, and continued deposit-cost discipline, holding NIM near-flat at 3.66%. Non-interest income was little changed as a $40 million securities-repositioning loss offset a record wealth-management quarter (+6% q/q) and higher card/ATM fees. Expenses rose 5% q/q on higher incentive-linked salaries and outside-services timing, pushing the reported efficiency ratio to 58.3% (56.9% adjusted). Net charge-offs fell 12bp q/q to 0.42% of average loans, non-performing loans declined, and CET1 held at 10.7%. The company repurchased $59 million of stock, paid $226 million in common dividends, and raised its quarterly dividend 13% to $0.30/share. No numeric forward guidance was given for Q3 or FY2026.

drivers.explanation: CEO John Turner cited strategic execution and solid delivery giving the company momentum into the second half of 2026, citing market growth, local-market expertise, and technology investment.
